facility: Williams Geismar Olefins Plant, propylene fractionator reboiler rupture and fire, Geismar, Louisiana, June 13, 2013
source: U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board, Williams Geismar Olefins Plant Reboiler Rupture and Fire, Case Study No. 2013-03-I-LA, October 2016 (public record)
question: On June 13, 2013, propylene fractionator Reboiler B at the Williams Geismar olefins plant ruptured about three minutes after an operations supervisor opened the hot quench water (about 187 F) to its tubes; it had been offline on standby for 16 months since maintenance in February 2012. Shell side process fluid: about 95% propane, balance mostly propylene and C4s. Reboiler B shell design: maximum allowable working pressure 300 psig, hydrostatic test 450 psig. Using the facility description, the schematic and the incident timeline, determine the failure mechanism and estimate with calculations the pressures that could be reached in the shell, explain why the reboiler was not protected from overpressure, and recommend the design, procedural and management changes that would prevent a recurrence.

definitions.definition: Distillation column in olefins process that separates reaction products into individual components; cooled furnace effluent gases go to series of distillation columns, such as the propylene fractionator, which separate the reaction products (p.7).

Shell and tube heat exchangers where tube-side hot quench water vaporizes shell-side hydrocarbon process fluid, approximately 95% propane with balance mostly propylene and C4s; report refers to mixture as 'propane' (p.9).

Closed-loop water circulation that directly contacts heated furnace effluent gases in quench tower, sprayed downward from top; heated quench water serves as heat source in various heat exchangers heating process streams, then cooled by cooling water system before returning to quench tower (p.7). Includes quench water settler that removes most oily tar products (p.8).

Buildup of oily tar material that condenses into quench water and adheres to inside of process equipment such as heat exchanger tubes, resulting in decrease in both heat transfer efficiency and quench water flow rate (p.8).

Design pressure rating stamped on vessel; for Reboiler B shell provided as 300 psig in assignment brief (pending verification on pages >13, not in p.6-13). Withheld clause in p.9 relates to 2001 modification.
Shop/field test at 1.5x MAWP per ASME; for Reboiler B shell provided as 450 psig in assignment brief (1.5x300).

In 2001 Williams installed valves on shell-side and tube-side reboiler piping to allow continuous operation with only one reboiler operating at a time. Other reboiler would be offline but ready for operation, isolated from process by new valves, allowing cleaning of fouled reboiler while fractionator continued to operate (p.9). Valves isolating reboilers from pressure relief valve at top of propylene fractionator were not part of original design and were installed in 2001 (p.10).

Rapid overpressure rupture due to heating of trapped/blocked-in shell-side liquid propane by hot quench water introduced to tubes after 16-month standby with isolation valves closed, eliminating relief path.

rfi.item: RFI-01: Quench water inlet temperature discrepancy
rfi.issue: p.9 states "approximately 185 °F" while task brief states "about 187 F"; impacts propane vapor pressure calculation and thermal expansion assessment.
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Adopt range 185-187 F for analysis, use 187 F as conservative upper bound for pressure estimates. Reason: Both described as approximate; difference within measurement/operating variation; using higher temperature bounds worst-case overpressure.
rfi.reason: No calibrated temperature trend provided in p.6-13; need field DCS historian accuracy.

rfi.issue: 300 psig MAWP and 450 psig hydrotest provided only in brief; not quoted in p.6-13 (p.9 indicates withheld detail). No nameplate, U-1A, or design datasheet available in excerpt.
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Accept 300 psig MAWP / 450 psig hydrotest per brief as correct pending verification; ratios consistent with ASME 1.5x hydrotest. Treat as design basis for overpressure margin discussion.
rfi.reason: Withheld Section 5.1 and later pages not available; standard vessel documentation not in excerpt.

rfi.item: RFI-03: Shell-side isolation status and trapped inventory
rfi.issue: p.9 says other reboiler would be offline but ready, isolated by new valves (installed 2001); p.10 confirms gate valves isolating reboilers from fractionator relief valve. Not specified whether Reboiler B shell inlet/outlet block valves were closed trapping liquid propane during 16-month standby, whether drain/vent valves were left open, or whether valves leaked.
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Reboiler B shell was blocked-in with liquid propane trapped (both inlet/condensate return and vapor outlet block valves closed, vents/drains closed) for entire 16 months, with no thermal relief. Reason: Described standby "isolated from the process by the new valves" (p.9) and explosion ~3 min after heating implies bulk liquid heating/boiling in sealed volume; leakage would have pressurized to fractionator pressure and not remained liquid-full.
rfi.reason: Critical to determine liquid-full hydraulic vs. vapor-space boiling mechanism; no valve position log or P&ID in excerpt.

rfi.issue: p.10 states isolating valves were not part of original design; Fig.4 schematic (not fully legible) shows isolating reboilers from relief at top of propylene fractionator. Unknown if Reboiler B was connected to any other relief device (e.g., dedicated thermal relief) when isolated, or if operators understood relief was defeated.
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: When isolated, Reboiler B shell had NO pressure relief path - neither to fractionator overhead PSV nor dedicated thermal PSV. Reason: CSB highlighting of 2001 valves as causal factor (p.10) and fact that vessel ruptured below hydrotest-equivalent pressure indicates absence of adequate relief; original design relied on common column relief.
rfi.reason: Relief sizing basis, PSV set pressure, capacity not in p.6-13; need Section 5.1.

rfi.item: RFI-05: Fractionator operating pressure and PSV set point
rfi.issue: Normal operating pressure of propylene fractionator / reboiler shell not given; PSV set pressure unknown. Affects initial condition before heating (saturated propane at operating T/P vs. atmospheric).
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Normal shell-side condition ~130 °F saturated propane (~200 psig vapor pressure at that T). Reason: p.9 shell inlet ~130 °F partially vaporizes propane; typical C3 fractionator reboiler pressure ~150-250 psig; starting point below MAWP but above atmospheric, consistent with 3-min rapid rise to rupture.
rfi.reason: No DCS pressure trend in excerpt; need PFD/operating manual.

rfi.item: RFI-06: Shell liquid full vs. vapor space condition at heating
rfi.issue: Whether Reboiler B shell was 100% liquid-full (hydraulic expansion case) or contained vapor pad (boiling pressure rise limited to vapor pressure at quench temperature) changes predicted pressure by orders of magnitude.
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Primary case liquid-full or near-liquid-full with small vapor bubble compressed to nil, leading to hydraulic/near-hydraulic pressure exceeding MAWP within minutes; alternate bounding case saturated propane vapor pressure at quench water temperature (~185-187 F) also exceeds MAWP. Reason: 16-month standstill allows condensation/cooling and accumulation; vessel orientation and trapped condensate scenario typical.
rfi.reason: No level, pre-startup vent procedure, or field measurement in excerpt.

rfi.item: RFI-07: Propane vapor pressure curve for actual mixture (95% C3 / C4 / C3=)
rfi.issue: p.9 mixture ~95% C3; pure propane vapor pressure vs. temperature needed for quantitative pressure estimate; C4s shift bubble point slightly. No tabulated data in excerpt.
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Use pure propane saturation properties as proxy; mixture bubble point slightly higher than pure propane but within ~2-5% for 95% purity. Reason: Sufficient for order-of-magnitude demonstration that saturation pressure at 185-187 F exceeds 300 psig MAWP.
rfi.reason: Need lab composition or simulator EOS; not in p.6-13.

rfi.item: RFI-08: Operating procedure for standby reboiler startup
rfi.issue: No SOP described for commissioning offline reboiler (pre-warming, venting, pressure equalization, gradual quench introduction, requirement to open vapor return before hot water). Supervisor acted without operations manager available (p.11).
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: No formal procedure existed or it was not used; decision was informal troubleshooting to "switch reboilers" without MOC/PSM review. Reason: p.11 describes nonroutine operational activity and ad-hoc supervisor action when manager unavailable; indicates procedural gap.
rfi.reason: Need SOP manual, training records, MOC for 2001 change - not in excerpt.

rfi.issue: Whether Reboiler B shell had prior thinning, corrosion, or damage from 16-month idle (e.g., CUI, fouling under-deposit) that lowered burst pressure.
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Shell burst essentially at defect-free pressure between MAWP and hydrotest, driven purely by overpressure; ignore pre-damage for pressure estimation, note for recommendation. Reason: CSB focus on overpressure vs. relief isolation (p.10-11) rather than corrosion; no inspection data in excerpt.
rfi.reason: Need inspection/MT records, metallurgy - not in p.6-13.

test_plan.acceptance: Timeline 08:33 open to ~08:36 rupture corroborated; absence/inadequacy of formal standby reboiler startup procedure and MOC for relief isolation documented as root cause

test_plan.test: Non-destructive testing of Reboiler B remnant and Reboiler A analogue
test_plan.purpose: Close RFI-09 and validate failure pressure estimate
test_plan.measurements: Visual/fractography, UT thickness, hardness, Charpy of shell material; burst pressure calculation per ASME vs. hydrotest 450 psig; comparison to saturation pressure at 187 F (~400-550 psig range for propane)
test_plan.procedure: Lab exam of ruptured sections (Fig.7/8) for ductile overload vs. pre-existing defect; review MT/UT records from Feb 2012 maintenance; calc thin-wall hoop stress at MAWP/hydro/saturation pressure

findings.modification: Recommended: B1 MOC per OSHA 1910.119(l) + PHA per 1910.119(e) including API 521 blocked-in/thermal scenarios for 2001 valves, PSSR 1910.119(m), fleet audit of exchangers with isolation valves; A1 add dedicated PSV per API 521/520 + P&ID update to CSO/blind for maintenance; B2 formal standby switching SOP with two-person verification, gradual pre-warm (open vapor first), manager approval, DCS permissive quench vs shell block position, fouling monitoring triggers vs hot-swap.

findings.unit: PSM management system - human factors / 16-month standby equipment without procedure
findings.limiting_value: Nonroutine reboiler switch performed alone without SOP, without operations manager p.11, on equipment offline 16 months p.7/Task brief with unknown trapped liquid pressure - organizational failure. Plant down 18 months to Jan 2015 p.12, 3.5-hr fire p.12.
findings.evidence: p.11 group analyzed data after manager noted flow drop; supervisor relied on to troubleshoot; decided to switch reboilers and opened valves per Fig.6. No procedure described for bringing offline reboiler online, no vent/drain verification. 16-month dormancy with closed blocks p.9 implies no preservation/inspection. Quench 185°F p.9 vs 187°F Task brief ±2°F both exceed limits per recalibrated gauge comparison.
findings.modification: Recommended: B1-B2 PSM upgrades - operating procedure 1910.119(f) for standby/temporarily isolated equipment, training, MOC, PHA, PSSR, audit; share lessons; implement DCS interlock + toolbox talk on blocked-in thermal expansion hazard per API 521; estimated one-time $100-300k for PHA/MOC overhaul vs 18-month outage loss.

alternatives.unit: Reboiler B shell - overpressure protection (defeated relief)
alternatives.option: A1 - Dedicated ASME VIII thermal/relief valve(s) on each reboiler shell set ≤300 psig to flare/overhead, sized per API 521 blocked-in heat input + liquid expansion (requires formal orifice calc and flare header verification)
alternatives.result: Conceptually limits shell to ~110% MAWP per API 520 accumulation; Psat 480-490 psig at 185-187°F fully relieved; hydraulic 10-14 bar/K rise relieved by small orifice but must be verified by calculation. Most robust engineered control.
alternatives.cost_basis: 2x PSVs (typ. 1.5-3in) + piping to flare + engineering/MOC indicative $150-400k installed; flare verification extra if undersized - estimate not sourced, requires quote

alternatives.unit: Reboiler B shell - overpressure protection (defeated relief)
alternatives.option: A2 - Revert to original intent: remove gate isolation valves p.10 Fig.4 or keep car-sealed open with blinds/spades for maintenance, restoring communication to column overhead PSV
alternatives.result: Shell remains tied to fractionator PSV; trapped volume eliminated. Prevents overpressure but reintroduces p.9 drawback of fractionator downtime for cleaning when fouled p.8.
alternatives.cost_basis: Valve removal/blinds + P&ID/CSO hardware + MOC indicative $15-40k - estimate

alternatives.unit: Reboiler B shell - trapped liquid prevention
alternatives.option: A3 - Standby de-inventory/vent procedure: offline reboiler drained, depressured, N2 purged, vent/drain locked open to safe containment, verified empty; DCS interlock prohibits quench valves unless shell blocks closed + vent open + pressure low
alternatives.result: Eliminates inventory to pressurize; interlock would have blocked 08:33 p.11 action. Requires disciplined ops, paired with A1 for defense-in-depth.
alternatives.cost_basis: SOP rewrite + DCS logic + N2 station + training indicative $30-80k per PSM 1910.119(d)/(f)

alternatives.option: B1 - Revalidate MOC 1910.119(l) and PHA 1910.119(e) for 2001 valve addition including API 521 scenarios; PSSR 1910.119(m); fleet audit for trapped-liquid exchangers
alternatives.result: PHA would have identified isolating shell from PSV creates 480-490 psig > MAWP/hydrotest hazard; mandates A1/A2 before approval. Addresses CSB 2013-03-I-LA systemic finding.
alternatives.cost_basis: Third-party PHA revalidation + MOC overhaul + fleet screening indicative $100-300k one-time vs 18-month outage p.12

alternatives.option: B2 - Formal SOP: two-person verification, pre-warm with vapor return open first, pressure equalization, gradual quench with T monitoring, manager approval; DCS permissive quench vs shell isolation
alternatives.result: Procedural + hard interlock prevents hot water to blocked-in shell; Fig.6 rapid flow increase at 08:33 p.11 blocked until path open.
alternatives.cost_basis: SOP + DCS logic + simulator training indicative $20-60k
